title: Weak Sobolev spaces of real bundle sections and finite-chart norms
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a smooth $m$-manifold without boundary [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], and let $B\to N$ be a smooth rank-$q$ real vector bundle [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle] with a smooth fibre metric. Use smooth sections in the sense of [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-sections]. A smooth tangent metric $g$ determines metric volume $\mu$ by the chart formula $c_*(\mu|_{U})=\sqrt{\det G_c}\,dy|_{c(U)}$, where $G_c$ is its Gram matrix on the inverse-chart coordinate tangent vectors. A finite oriented coordinate trivializing cover is a finite family of smooth charts $c_i:U_i\to V_i$ covering $N$, positive transition Jacobian determinants, smooth bundle frames on neighborhoods of $U_i$, and a smooth subordinate partition of unity $\chi_i$ with closed support inside $U_i$, as in [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition]. Define $L^2(B,\mu)$ as the almost-everywhere equivalence classes of Borel-measurable sections (allowing almost-everywhere measurable representatives) with $\int_N\|s(x)\|^2d\mu<\infty$, and $\|v\|_{L^2}=(\int_N\|v(x)\|^2d\mu)^{1/2}$. On an open coordinate domain $V$, a scalar coefficient $f$ has weak derivative $d_\alpha$ if $d_\alpha$ is measurable and locally square integrable and $\int_V d_\alpha\phi=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_V f\partial^\alpha\phi$ for every smooth compactly supported real coefficient test in $V$ [def-sfb-local-coefficient-tests]. Let $H^0(B,\mu)=L^2(B,\mu)$; for $j>0$, $H^j(B,\mu)$ is the subset of these same classes whose coefficients in every smooth chart and bundle frame are locally square integrable and have locally square-integrable weak derivatives for all multi-indices $|\alpha|\leq j$. Localized coefficients are $w_{ik}(y)=\chi_i(c_i^{-1}y)(s\text{ in frame }i)_k(c_i^{-1}y)$ on $V_i$ and zero outside. For $j>0$ define $\|v\|_{H^j}=(\sum_{i,k}\sum_{|\alpha|\leq j}\int_{\mathbf R^m}|\partial^\alpha w_{ik}|^2dy)^{1/2}$, and for $j=0$ use $\|v\|_{L^2}$. Weak derivatives are selected from their test identities, which determine them up to almost-everywhere equality; no numerical norm depends on that selection or the representative. These are concrete subsets of the dependent almost-everywhere quotient, not abstract completions or unspecified spaces.
